subject: Mutual close runway & conformance checklist
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Clara Ruiz <clara.ruiz@medivue.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mutual close runway & conformance checklist

Clara — thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation I put together a pragmatic mutual action plan (attached) that focuses the next 2 weeks on the core acceptance tests we need to validate for a production pilot. High level asks below; details in the MAP and acceptance-test matrix (attached).

Quick summary / asks:
- Redwood deliverables (by Jun 30): updated integration shim, evaluation AM/PM smoke run, acceptance-test matrix results for 500 sample interactions, SOC2 evidence pointer.
- Medivue deliverables: provide test dataset subset (de-identified) + service-level test account by Jun 23; procurement to confirm terms by Jun 26.
- Success criteria (pass/fail): see Acceptance Tests section — key gates are functional conformance, latency/SLA, and data handling verification.

Exit gates (short):
1) Functional – 95% of sample prompts return correct structured output per schema.
2) Performance – p95 inference latency < 250ms on trial load; ability to sustain 50 QPS for 10 minutes without errors.
3) Security/compliance – KMS integration verified; sample audit log present for 7 days retention.

Immediate next steps:
- Clara: confirm who from procurement will own redlines (cc procurement in reply).
- Karthik: can you own the smoke-run checklist and assign the QA owner?
- Jordan: will coordinate the canary schedule and DocuSign wrap.

Attachments: Medivue_MAP_v2.xlsx (map + task owners), acceptance-test-matrix.md (detailed tests + pass thresholds)

Thanks — Sean

Sean — appreciate the concise plan. A few clarifications before we commit:
- The sample dataset: we'll provide a 1,200-record de-identified set; can you confirm format expectations and the secure drop method?
- Latency gate: Medivue's internal SLO for production is p95 < 200ms. Is that target achievable with the trial config, or should we explicitly call out a staged threshold?
- Procurement: looping them in — Derek (copied) will lead the contract redlines and timing.

If possible, can you indicate which acceptance tests require production-like traffic vs. which can run on a smaller dev pool? That will help us prioritize infra scheduling on our side.

Thanks,

Thanks Clara — answers inline and an update to the gates below.

On Tue, Jun 17, 2025 at 11:05 AM Clara Ruiz <clara.ruiz@medivue.com> wrote:
> Sean — appreciate the concise plan. A few clarifications before we commit:
> - The sample dataset: we'll provide a 1,200-record de-identified set; can you confirm format expectations and the secure drop method?

We can accept a CSV or NDJSON. Preferred: NDJSON with a top-level id and fields: prompt, expected_schema_json. For secure transfer use the Drive link I shared (Drive folder with enforced access). I will also share a temporary S3 presigned URL if you prefer direct upload.

> - Latency gate: Medivue's internal SLO for production is p95 < 200ms. Is that target achievable with the trial config, or should we explicitly call out a staged threshold?

Recommend staged thresholds for evaluation:
- Evaluation pass: p95 < 250ms on trial pool (non-prewarmed)
- Pilot readiness: p95 < 200ms on dedicated pool with warm KV cache and batching tuned

We'll explicitly record both gates in the MAP so there is no ambiguity.

> - If possible, can you indicate which acceptance tests require production-like traffic vs. which can run on a smaller dev pool?

Acceptance-test quick mapping:
- Functional conformance (schema checks, field-level validation): small dev pool (sample dataset)
- Safety checks and PII scan: small dev pool + static ruleset
- Load & latency: production-like or dedicated pilot pool (50 QPS sustained)
- End-to-end instrumentation / audit log verification: dedicated pilot pool

Updated exit gates (excerpt):
- Gate A - Functional: 95% pass on schema/intent for 500-sample randomized subset (dev pool)
- Gate B - Performance: p95 < 250ms (eval pool); p95 < 200ms for pilot readiness (dedicated)
- Gate C - Compliance: KMS + audit logs validated; documented data lifecycle for retention and deletion tested

I'll attach a short smoke checklist (acceptance-test-matrix.md) and flag the items that require a dedicated pool. Karthik — can you own the dev-pool test run early next week?

— Sean
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Clara Ruiz <clara.ruiz@medivue.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Final MAP + conformance checklist (next steps + signature)

Clara — quick update and next steps. Per Sean's edits we've versioned the MAP to Medivue_MAP_v2.xlsx and embedded a clear pass/fail column in the acceptance-test-matrix.md. Summary of final items and responsibilities below.

Key pass criteria (finalized):
- Functional conformance: >= 95% field-level correctness for the 500-sample evaluation set (automated schema checks + manual review of top 50 failures).
- Behavioral: no high-severity safety regressions across 1,200+ prompts sampled; documented remediation plan for any regression.
- Performance: evaluation p95 < 250ms (eval pool). Pilot readiness requires p95 < 200ms on dedicated pool with warm caches. Error rate < 0.5% during trials.
- Observability & audit: request-level audit logs available for sample timeframe; KMS key rotation test executed.

Exit gates and acceptance tests (owners):
- Gate A (Functional) — Owner: Karthik Iyer — run schema validator, produce report (artifact: acceptance-test-matrix.md -> functional tab).
- Gate B (Performance) — Owner: Grace O'Connor — run load test (50 QPS sustained x 10m), collect p95 and error rate.
- Gate C (Security/Compliance) — Owner: Sean Gallagher — verify KMS + audit logs, provide pointer to SOC2 evidence.

Schedule / timeline:
- Jun 18: procurement to share redlines (Derek)
- Jun 20: dev-pool functional run (Karthik)
- Jun 24: performance run in eval pool (Grace)
- Jun 26: procurement sign (target)
- Jun 30: pilot canary (if Gates A–C pass)

Attachments included in this thread: Medivue_MAP_v2.xlsx, acceptance-test-matrix.md. Also shared DocuSign envelope: https://docusign.com/envelopes/MDV-1193. Please reply with approval or requested edits; if procurement requires a later signature window we can shift the pilot date accordingly.

Thanks — Jordan
